column1: # Australia: Diyanet's Sydney table (diy-syd, 25 September to 25 October 2026, the TURKEY preset to within a minute:
# 7g's proof) against Diyanet's preset chosen on its own (other.turkey). The owner's decision of 17 Oct 2026 (question
# 4): someone in Sydney who picks Diyanet means the Turkish mosques' timetable, so the preset is never before it, nor
# any end after it. Diyanet does not publish the table's point, so it is read at each plausible one, the points the
# preset rides beside the user's own (Americas.sydneyDiyanetPoints, as au.cautious's member does): Lakemba, where
# au-cautious.tsv reads it; Sydney's centre, the app's own Sydney, where Diyanet's city tables usually sit; and the
# Gallipoli Mosque at Auburn, the Turkish community's. Measured: a user who chooses Diyanet here follows this table,
# so its lateness is theirs, held to class D's limit (other.turkey claims no figure in About all the same). The app's
# other cities where the chosen preset rides the three points are au-diyanet-envelope.tsv's promise-only rows. Maghrib
# is checked, as every start. No imsak is printed: each Fajr is also the start of the fast.
# Every row is held out.
# These are the only days of the table the archive holds: no fetcher reads Diyanet's Australian pages, so prove never
# grows these rows, and a capture from another season is added by hand. Until one is, "never before it" is proven for
# these 31 days only; the other months rest on the preset being Diyanet's own rule, never before Diyanet's tables at its
# six published points in tr-diyanet.tsv. On these days every start is at least a minute after the table and every end
# at least a minute before it, the same at all three points, since each rides the other two. Asr is 2 to 3 min after
# it, at class D's limit on 26 of the 31 days: a capture that comes out a minute later breaks the gate, which then asks
# for a reason (R41) or a fix.
